chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a slave girl whom he would have sexual relations with, and news reached him that she had a husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can have sexual relations with her, for her sale is her divorce, and that is because they are both unable to do anything regarding their matter when they are sold.'

key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He has sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man buying a slave girl who is already married?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'bay'uhu talāquhā' (her sale is her divorce), establishing that the separation of the slave couple from their original master dissolves their marital bond, allowing the new owner to consummate the relationship immediately. It reflects the juristic view that the husband's right to cohabit is tied to the wife's availability within the master's household, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding concubinage and slavery. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan scholars, particularly Safwan ibn Yahya, in transmitting this practical legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS).
